🇮🇷🇺🇸 Iran just showed off a NEW MISSILE LAUNCHER. A rocket expert thinks it may reveal how much TROUBLE Tehran is in.

Brandon Weichert spoke with missile specialist Dr. Markus Schiller about Iran's underground twin-missile launcher and its claims of reaching targets 5,000 kilometers away.

Schiller wasn't particularly impressed.

The missiles shown appear to be older Scud-derived designs, with an estimated range of just 800–1,000 kilometers.

And their accuracy is poor.

They could still threaten Gulf airbases, power plants and other large targets, but hitting a moving warship would be another matter entirely.

The more interesting detail is the launcher itself.

By carrying two missiles instead of one, Iran could maintain its firing capacity with fewer surviving launchers.

Schiller thinks that could be a sign Tehran is running short of launch equipment.

He also questioned how long Iran can sustain its missile campaign.

Open-source estimates suggest Iran has already fired 1,300–1,800 ballistic missiles. Replacing them requires engines, guidance systems, specialized materials and production facilities that may already be under pressure.

Nobody outside Tehran knows the real numbers.

And Schiller cautioned against assuming Iran can overwhelm American aircraft carriers. Its missiles pose a genuine threat to ships operating near the Strait of Hormuz, but coordinating a large enough attack against a heavily defended carrier is considerably harder.

We also discussed Russia's increasingly effective jet-powered drones in Ukraine, nuclear-capable missiles stationed in Kaliningrad and the industrial weakness of Western weapons production.

America builds extraordinarily sophisticated weapons. Its adversaries often prioritize building ENOUGH weapons.

In a prolonged war, that difference matters enormously.

@WeTheBrandon @RocketSchiller
